styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Temples, the Old Quarter lanes and water puppets.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Pho, bun cha and street-side coffee crawls.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Ho Chi Minh's mausoleum, Hoa Lo and museums.

stays.why: Walk to Hoan Kiem Lake, street food and markets. Lively and loud; ask for a quiet room.
Wide tree-lined streets, the Opera House and quieter nights, a short walk from the lake.
Central and handy for the lake, the Old Quarter edge and evening walks.
Lakeside expat area with cafés and quieter streets; 15–25 minutes by taxi to the centre.

food: Start with pho for breakfast, bun cha at lunch and a bia hoi (fresh beer) corner in the evening.
Eat where locals sit: small stalls and family restaurants in the Old Quarter are often the best value.
Try egg coffee (ca phe trung) and strong drip coffee at a café near Hoan Kiem Lake.
Street food is cheap: expect roughly 30,000–80,000 VND for a bowl or plate; check on the day.
Drink bottled water and eat busy, freshly cooked stalls. Carry small notes for street vendors.
more_time: Swap a city day for Ha Long Bay or Lan Ha Bay: a long day trip or an overnight on a boat.
Take a half-day to the Temple of Literature and the Imperial Citadel if you like history.
Spend an afternoon in Tay Ho for lakeside cafés and a quieter side of Hanoi.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the Old Quarter, the lake and the main history sights, with time left for a street-food crawl.

month_notes: January: cool and dry, highs near 21°C. Bring a jacket for evenings.
February: mild and dry, around 22°C. Good walking weather.
March: warming to 26°C with more rain days. Pack a light rain layer.
April: warm at 29°C, some rain. Comfortable for sightseeing.
May: hot and humid at 32°C with frequent rain. Plan indoor breaks.
June: hot at 33°C and wet. Go out early and late.
July: hot and rainy, around 21 rain days. Keep plans flexible.
August: the wettest month, 24 rain days. Carry a raincoat.
September: still wet and warm at 31°C. Watch for heavy showers.
October: cooler at 28°C and drier. A pleasant month to visit.
November: mild at 26°C with fewer rain days. Great for walking.
December: cool and dry, highs near 21°C. Light layers needed.

climate_guide.summary: Subtropical Hanoi: mild, drier winters and hot, very wet summers. Rain peaks from July to September.

items.title: Best time: October to April
items.text: Milder days around 21–29°C and fewer rain days. Good for walking the Old Quarter.

items.title: Hot, humid summer (May to September)
items.text: Highs of 31–33°C with many rain days. Sightsee early morning and after showers.

items.title: Wettest months: July to September
items.text: Around 21–24 rain days a month. Showers can be heavy; keep a raincoat handy.

items.title: Cool winter (December to February)
items.text: Highs near 21–22°C and lows around 14–15°C. Bring a jacket for evenings.

items.title: Rain is often short
items.text: Even in wet months, showers pass. Plan indoor stops like museums and cafés as backup.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light layers, a raincoat or umbrella, comfortable shoes for uneven streets, and a warm layer for winter.

transit.best: Grab for cars and motorbike taxis; walk in the Old Quarter.

modes.text: Line 2A runs Cat Linh to Yen Nghia; Line 3 runs Cau Giay to Nhon. Fares are distance-based, about 8,000–15,000 VND; tap contactless cards at gates.
City buses are cheap and air-conditioned, about 7,000–12,000 VND per ride.
Grab works well for cars and motorbike taxis; fares are fixed in the app. Metered taxis: Mai Linh and Taxi Group are reliable; flag-fall about 20,000 VND.
Not practical for most visitors: chaotic traffic and hard parking. Use Grab or taxis instead.
Fine in the Old Quarter, but crossing takes nerve. Traffic is chaotic; take your time at crossings.
